entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zhao Mengjian, art name Yizhai (彝齋居士), was a Chinese painter and politician from Haiyan, Zhejiang, active during the Yuan dynasty (1271–1368).

As a prominent figure in the Yuan court, he played a key role in the transition from the Song to the Ming dynasty, collaborating with Kublai Khan and later serving as a governor of Zhejiang province.

Mengjian's artistic contributions include the creation of intricate landscape paintings, which showcased his unique blend of traditional Chinese styles and innovative techniques.

His legacy extends beyond the arts, as he helped shape the cultural and political landscape of Ming-era China, paving the way for the rise of the Ming dynasty.

'In the realm of painting, one must not be afraid to take risks, for it is in the pursuit of innovation that true mastery is achieved.' — Yizhai, as quoted in the Ming dynasty art collection of the Palace Museum, Beijing.
